name: Jane App vs TheraNest
title: Jane App vs TheraNest: Practice Management Comparison for Mental Health
description: Compare Jane App and TheraNest for mental health practices. See differences in pricing, features, telehealth, and mental health-specific capabilities.

summary.bottom_line: Jane App is a multi-disciplinary platform built for allied health with strong telehealth and AI, while TheraNest is purpose-built specifically for mental health with affordable per-therapist pricing. Choose Jane App for multi-disciplinary practices or those wanting AI documentation; choose TheraNest for mental health-only practices seeking affordable, therapy-specific workflows.

sections.heading: Jane App vs TheraNest: Overview
sections.content: Jane App and TheraNest both serve mental health practices but come from different backgrounds. Jane App was built in Canada for multi-disciplinary allied health clinics (physio, chiro, massage, psychology) and later expanded to mental health. TheraNest was built specifically for mental health from the start in 2008 and is now part of Ensora Health (formerly Therapy Brands). TheraNest offers more mental health-specific features like Wiley Treatment Planner integration, while Jane App offers broader multi-disciplinary flexibility and strong telehealth.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: TheraNest is generally more affordable for mental health practices with per-therapist pricing starting at $29/month (Essentials). Jane App starts at $54/month (Balance) for a single practitioner. For full features with telehealth, TheraNest Premier is $89/therapist/month while Jane App Thrive is $99/month. Both charge extra for AI documentation: Jane's AI Scribe is $15/mo, TheraNest's AI Session Assistant is $35/mo. TheraNest is typically the more budget-friendly option for therapy practices.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: TheraNest has the edge in mental health-specific features including Wiley Treatment Planner integration and therapy-specific note templates designed for behavioral health documentation. Jane App's strength is telehealth (included on all plans vs. TheraNest Premier only) and AI documentation (cheaper at $15 vs $35). Jane App is also better for practices that mix mental health with other disciplines. Both have client portals, online booking, and insurance billing capabilities.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your practice type and budget:

recommendations.when: You run a multi-disciplinary practice, want telehealth on all plans, prefer cheaper AI documentation, or are based in Canada
You're a mental health-only practice, want purpose-built therapy workflows, need Wiley Treatment Planner, or prefer lower per-therapist pricing
You're a solo therapist comparing overall value - both offer solid features at different price points

faqs.q: Is TheraNest better for therapists than Jane App?
faqs.a: TheraNest is purpose-built for mental health with therapy-specific features like Wiley Treatment Planner integration. Jane App is more versatile for multi-disciplinary practices. For therapy-only practices, TheraNest may feel more tailored to mental health workflows.

faqs.q: Which is cheaper for a solo therapist?
faqs.a: TheraNest Essentials at $29/month is cheaper than Jane App Balance at $54/month. However, for full features with telehealth, compare TheraNest Premier ($89) to Jane App Thrive ($99)—closer in price at the top tier.

faqs.q: Does Jane App have mental health-specific templates?
faqs.a: Jane App has general clinical note templates that can be customized for mental health, but TheraNest has more therapy-specific templates built by behavioral health clinicians, including Wiley Treatment Planner integration.
Jane App includes telehealth on all plans while TheraNest only includes it on the Premier plan ($89/month). For practices prioritizing telehealth, Jane App offers better value at lower tiers.
